_caveats.llm_cache_contamination: Layer 5 adapters (SmartLLM, GPTScan, GPTLens) are file-backed-cached by contract source hash at ~/.miesc/*_cache/ (24h TTL, see miesc/adapters/_cache_mixin.py). This run reused cached results for a subset of contracts (touched by an earlier --limit 2 smoke test run minutes before, and possibly by the original 2026-08-14 investigation of AuctionDemo.sol for item #5). Three subsequent attempts to reproduce this run with MIESC_DISABLE_LLM_CACHE=1 for a fully fresh measurement were killed by the environment (background execution instability unrelated to the workload - Ollama and system load were verified healthy) before completing. Effect on these numbers: avg_time_s for layer 5 (65.007s) is likely an UNDERESTIMATE of true per-contract cost (cache hits return in 0.0s, pulling the average down); TP/FP counts are not fabricated by the cache (it replays a genuine prior real output for the same source hash), so detection outcomes are still real, just not independently re-verified fresh in this exact run. Layers 1, 3, 7, and 9 do not use this cache (no LLM calls, or - for layer 9 - no upstream findings to act on in standalone ablation mode) and are unaffected.
_caveats.layer5_fallback_dominance: Log evidence (see ablation_run_20260815.log) shows the bulk of layer 5's per-contract evaluations did NOT complete real LLM inference within the 60s timeout: LlamaAudit fell back to pattern-based analysis on 20/20 contract-evaluations (100%), iAudit's planner fell back to pattern analysis on 20/20 (100%), LLM-SmartAudit used text-parsing fallback on 18/20, and GPTScan/GPTLens mixed fallback and cache hits. This means layer 5's reported precision/recall substantially reflects the SAME kind of pattern-based heuristic detection as layer 1, not genuine LLM reasoning - which is the direct explanation for why layer 5's true-positive set is byte-identical to layer 1's and layer 9's (see MEJORAS2.md #5c). A fair measurement of AI's real marginal value would need a larger timeout, a faster/local model, or a cloud LLM budget - none of which this environment (Ollama over LAN at 192.168.0.197, qwen2.5-coder:7b-16k) supports within a 60s-per-tool budget.
